final_rationale: The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; the response mainly narrowed the claim and aligned it more tightly to the existing record. That matters here. The policy text says certification without material caveats requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The available summary indicates neither is present. But the Actor no longer argues that draft monitoring cures that gap or that no material limitation remains. Instead, the Actor limits the position to certification only with explicit disclosure of the known credit-underwriting limitation and correction of the model-card language. On the present record, that narrower, policy-bounded position is supportable as compliant_with_caveats. The distinction is that the caveat is not a substitute for the unresolved weakness; it is the condition that keeps the certification argument from overstating compliance. Clean compliance remains unsupported.
remaining_concerns: The open credit-underwriting weakness remains a material limitation for a named launch use case.
The draft monitoring and rollback runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for removing a current disclosure requirement because key approval elements remain unresolved.
The current model-card statement that there are no known material limitations is not supportable and must be corrected.
The compliant path is conditional: certification is only supportable with explicit disclosure and caveated framing, not as clean certification.
